t:
(a) 
Section 102(c) of the Housing Act of 1949 is amended—

        (1) 
by striking out “at interest, rates lower than provided in the loan contract” in the first sentence; and
 
        (2) 
by inserting before the period at the end of the first sentence the following: “: Provided, That, if at any time during the undertaking of the project, the interest rate on such a loan from a source other than the Federal Government is greater than the rate at which funds could lie made available under the Federal loan contract, the Secretary may make a supplemental grant to the local public agency in the amount of the difference between the interest cost from such sources and the interest cost at the contract rate, and no part of the amount of any such grant shall be required to be contributed as a part of the local grant-in-aid”.
  
    (b) 
Loan contracts outstanding on the date of enactment of this section may be amended to incorporate the provisions authorized by the amendment contained in subsection (a) without regard to the proviso in section 110(g) of the Housing Act of 1949.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that mention of a "local public agency" and loan contracts signals coordination with a non-federal entity. But the section only authorizes a supplemental grant to cover interest-rate differences and permits amending existing loan contracts; grants and contracts are financial assistance, not consultation in a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: the Secretary may make a supplemental grant to the local public agency in the amount of the difference between the interest cost from such sources and the interest cost at the contract rate

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the Secretary to provide a supplemental grant to a local public agency based on interest rate differentials. It does not require consultation, coordination, or participation by the local agency or any other outside party in the decision-making process; it simply defines the conditions under which federal funds may be disbursed. The definition explicitly excludes applications for grants, and this text describes the grant mechanism itself, not a participatory process.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary may make a supplemental grant to the local public agency in the amount of the difference between the interest cost from such sources and the interest cost at the contract rate

opus.w: This section lets the Secretary make supplemental interest-rate grants to local public agencies and lets existing loan contracts be amended. A local agency receiving a grant or signing a contract falls under the excluded category of grants and contracts; it is not taking part in a federal decision. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue.
opus.s: the Secretary may make a supplemental grant to the local public agency in the amount of the difference between the interest cost from such sources and the interest cost at the contract rate
opus.b: 1. **Analysis.** The tempting reading is that this section involves an outside party, the "local public agency," and lets outstanding loan contracts with it be amended, which could look like the government coordinating with a local government. That reading fails. The local agency is only the recipient of a supplemental grant and a party to a loan contract. The definition excludes grants and contracts. Nothing here requires a comment period, rulemaking, a hearing, an advisory body or consultation before the Secretary decides, and nothing gives anyone a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section describes the conditions under which a federal grant can be made to a local agency. Applying for or receiving a grant is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation. It looks like participation because it involves a "local public agency" receiving a grant.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary may make a supplemental grant to the local public agency in the amount of the difference between the interest cost from such sources and the interest cost at the contract rate
